- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.6) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and forecast is rising, cap the forecast at 1–2% below the recent 5-day average to prevent overcorrection.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong mean reversion (prices trending down from a peak), adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to reflect momentum.  
- When sentiment is neutral (0.2–0.6) and forecast is consistently above true outcome, apply a 3–5% downward bias to avoid overconfidence.  
- If sentiment history shows a recent reversal (e.g., from +0.8 to -0.4), reduce forecast slope and add a 1–3% lagged correction to the next 5 days.
